name: Make an Object
about: Describe a thing (add a photo or drawing if you like) and Claude makes it as an Object: its 2D symbol and 3D primitive. In a project you keep it there, and can have its detailed version made next (Detail an Object); in the studio you propose it to the Library. Since 2.0.0 Innowa makes it with you in the chat (R115): ask for a change and it is made straight away.

input.about: What to make: its name, sizes and how it looks; photos or drawings help.

rules.text: Agents never change the Library or the project's model. They write the run's Needs, matches and draft Objects; only the owner's decisions change the project.
A made Object passes the Library check: its 2D symbol and 3D primitive agree at every parameter setting, every parameter has limits and changes something, sizes are whole millimetres.
A made Object is a Project Object: its id is project.<name>@1.0.0 and it stays in the project until the owner asks for it to be proposed to the Library.
Measure in millimetres. When a size is not given, use a usual size for the kind of thing and say so in the Need's notes.

steps.name: Make
steps.outcome: The thing described is an Object whose 2D symbol and 3D primitive agree at every parameter setting.
instructions: Make Library-style Objects: JSON with id, name, contract, kind, behaves, about, params (defaults), limits (min, max, step for numbers; options for text), symbol2d and primitive3d. Find the Library Objects closest to what you are making (library_list, then library_get for two or three of them) and follow their form exactly.
Where what to make is unclear and it matters (no size for something sized to a room, two ways it could open), ask the owner in the chat first: one short question, then make it.

Before you make each Need, open the page or photo its evidence cites with the Read tool, and read what the reader saw and why the matcher found nothing that fits. Make what the brief shows, not a generic version: its parts, how it opens, its materials (pick each part's slot to match the real material). Follow the owner's comments if there are any.

The local frame: millimetres, origin at the centre of the footprint on the floor, x to the right, y to the Object's front, z up. Every number may be a formula of the parameters ("width - 2 * leg"), read by a small parser: + - * / % ( ) comparisons, && || ! ?:, and min max abs round floor ceil sqrt clamp. A shape or part may repeat with count (i = 0..n-1, n) or be conditional with when.

symbol2d shapes: rect {at:[x,y], size:[w,d]}, line {from, to}, circle {at, r}, arc {at, r, start, end}, polyline {points, closed}; style fill (the outline), outline, hidden (dashed) or thin. primitive3d parts: box {at:[x,y,z], size:[w,d,h]} and cylinder {at:[x,y,z], size:[diameter, h]}, z the bottom of the part; give each part a slot (frame, seat, fabric, wood, metal, mattress, concrete, glass).

The 2D symbol must cover the same footprint as the 3D primitive at every parameter setting, every number parameter needs limits, and every parameter must change something. Parameter names are lower case with underscores and must not be i, n, true, false or a function name (for example not round).

The id is project.<short-name>@1.0.0 and the contract project.<short-name>, both lower case with hyphens (for example project.window-seat). Its kind is its word, usually furniture. behaves says what it does, from band, holds-openings, opening, way-through, stops-bands and cuts-floor-above: [] for anything that only stands where it is put (furniture, a fixture); a door is ["opening", "way-through"], a window ["opening"], a wall ["band", "holds-openings"].

Use library_check on your draft and fix every finding before you save it with object_put {need, object}. object_put runs the same check and refuses a failing Object. Save one Object per Need you were asked to make; then tell the owner in a sentence or two what you made, its parameters and their limits, and anything you assumed (a size the brief did not give).
If the run was sent back, the owner's comments (step_get) say what to change: change exactly that, keep the rest, and save again.

steps.name: Keep
steps.question: Keep these Objects in the project? They are pinned to it, ready to attach to a line, face or point; they stay out of the Library until you ask for them to be proposed. Not right? Write what to do differently and send it back.

steps.name: Propose to the Library
steps.question: Propose these Objects to the Library? Each goes by its own Propose to Library run (a pull request you merge). Not right? Write what to change and send it back.

output.name: Made Objects
output.about: The Object made and whether it was kept.

useWhen: The owner describes one thing to make (with a photo or drawing if they have one) and wants it as an Object in the project.
